chatSession.description: BuilderForce coding agent, as its own tab
config.baseUrl.desc: Base URL of the BuilderForce gateway. Defaults to the primary domain (`https://builderforce.ai/gateway`), which works on corporate networks that whitelist the main site but block the `api.` subdomain. The OpenAI-compatible endpoint `/llm/v1/chat/completions` is appended automatically. Override for self-hosted deployments or to call `https://api.builderforce.ai` directly.
config.webUrl.desc: Base URL of the BuilderForce web app (where embedded pages like the board live). Leave empty to derive it from `builderforce.baseUrl` (api.* → root domain).
config.defaultModel.desc: Default model id to use. Leave empty to let the gateway pick from the curated coding pool.
config.localModels.enabled.desc: Serve models from THIS machine instead of the BuilderForce gateway, and offer them in the model picker. Two kinds: an on-device runtime (Ollama, FreeToken, Synapse), where inference runs on your hardware, nothing reaches any provider, and it works offline; and a signed-in Kimi Code install, where VS Code calls Kimi directly with the account you already authenticated in Kimi Code — the request still goes to Kimi, but from your machine rather than our cloud, which is the personal client that subscription is licensed for. Neither consumes plan usage. The sidebar chat still saves its transcript to your BuilderForce account as usual.
config.localModels.ollamaUrl.desc: Base URL of your Ollama runtime. The OpenAI-compatible paths `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions` are appended automatically, so both `http://127.0.0.1:11434` and `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` work.
config.localModels.freetokenUrl.desc: Base URL of your FreeToken engine. The OpenAI-compatible paths `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions` are appended automatically, so both `http://127.0.0.1:1919` and `http://127.0.0.1:1919/v1` work.
config.localModels.synapseUrl.desc: Base URL of Synapse's native engine (`bfi serve`). Leave empty to discover it: the Synapse desktop app publishes it, and a standalone `bfi serve` announces its port in `~/.builderforce/bfi.json` (it starts at 11434 and moves up when Ollama holds that port). Its API key is picked up from the same discovery. Both `http://127.0.0.1:11435` and `http://127.0.0.1:11435/v1` work.
config.localModels.localFirst.desc: Prefer a compatible model on THIS machine: the built-in engines first (WebLLM and the Builderforce engine on WebGPU, then Synapse), Ollama and FreeToken last. Gateway fallback requires the separate Gateway inference permission; explicit local pins always win.
config.localModels.skipConfidence.desc: Hybrid only: skip the local model for a turn when this machine's learned predictor is at least this sure it would fail (0–1). Higher tries local more often; the predictor acts only once it has trained and beats a coin.
config.localModels.explore.desc: Hybrid only: of the turns the predictor would skip, the share still tried on the local model (0–1), so a model that improves can win its turns back. 0 never retries a skipped turn locally.
config.inferenceMode.desc: Where models run. Leave unset for the default: **Hybrid** once signed in, **Local only** signed out. The `builderforce.platform.*` settings are advanced overrides of what this mode allows.
config.inferenceMode.hybrid: **Hybrid** (recommended) — this device first, then BuilderForce cloud when it needs to (the gateway puts the free tier first).
config.inferenceMode.localOnly: **Local only** — only models on this device. Nothing is sent to the BuilderForce gateway.
config.inferenceMode.specific: **Specific model** — the model you pick always runs: a cloud model, your connected accounts, Kimi Code or one local model.
config.inferenceMode.unset: Not chosen — Hybrid once signed in, Local only signed out. You are asked on your first signed-in turn.
config.platform.synchronize.desc: Advanced override of the Inference Mode setting — leave unset to follow the mode. Allow account synchronization to send and receive BuilderForce data in batches. No mode turns this on by itself; Local only keeps it off.
config.platform.gatewayInference.desc: Advanced override of the Inference Mode setting — leave unset to follow the mode. Allow model turns to use the BuilderForce gateway. Hybrid and Specific model turn this on; Local only keeps it off whatever this says.
config.platform.connectedFeatures.desc: Advanced override of the Inference Mode setting — leave unset to follow the mode. Allow explicitly used connected features to read BuilderForce data or open platform streams and frames. Local execution does not require this.
config.platform.modelDownloads.desc: Advanced override of the Inference Mode setting — leave unset to follow the mode. Allow downloading model assets. Capability checks never download assets automatically.
config.platform.directProviders.desc: Advanced override of the Inference Mode setting — leave unset to follow the mode. Allow direct requests to non-BuilderForce model providers. This is separate from BuilderForce API access.
config.platform.externalMcp.desc: Advanced override of the Inference Mode setting — leave unset to follow the mode. Allow connections to external MCP servers. Unsupported offline tools remain unavailable instead of using a server substitute.
config.platform.gitRemotes.desc: Advanced override of the Inference Mode setting — leave unset to follow the mode. Allow Git remote network operations. Local files and local Git history do not require this.
config.permissionMode.desc: How the agent applies changes to your workspace.
config.permissionMode.ask: Ask before applying each file edit or command (recommended).
config.permissionMode.acceptEdits: Apply file edits automatically without prompting.
config.sessionTabs.desc: How opening a session from the Sessions view uses editor tabs.
config.sessionTabs.reuse: Reuse a single chat tab, switching sessions inside it.
config.sessionTabs.perSession: Open each session in its own tab, so you can switch between chats like editor tabs. Each tab shows that session's live status (⏳ working, ❓ waiting on your answer).
config.reportErrors.desc: Send errors this extension catches to your BuilderForce workspace, so they appear in Quality alongside every other error. Off by default: with it off, errors are written only to the BuilderForce output channel and never leave this machine.
config.audits.atStartup: Run selected audits in background chats when this workspace opens.
config.audits.atClose: Run selected audits in the cloud when this workspace closes. Uses connected repository source; local edits are not uploaded. Interrupted submissions retry on next startup.
config.audits.selected: Audit types to run at startup and close.
config.models.plan.desc: Model for the **planning** stage of a run. Empty: the `ROLE_MODELS` env `plan` entry, else the gateway orders your models for planning. Applies while the run holds no model of its own (Auto, and `#builderforce.defaultModel#` empty).
config.models.code.desc: Model for the **coding** stage of a run. Empty: the `ROLE_MODELS` env `code` entry, else the gateway leads with your strongest coding model. Applies while the run holds no model of its own (Auto, and `#builderforce.defaultModel#` empty).
config.models.review.desc: Model for the **review** (verify) stage, after a run changed code. Always a different model from the one that wrote the change. Empty: the `ROLE_MODELS` env `verify` entry, else the gateway picks a cheaper capable reviewer.
config.models.subagent.desc: Model every **sub-agent** runs on, unless your model pick is explicit. Empty: the `ROLE_MODELS` entry for the sub-agent's role, else the gateway orders by that role.
config.pipeline.routing.desc: How runs are routed between the **full pipeline** (plan → code → review) and a **quick pass** (one coding pass, no planning or review stage). Writing "full pipeline" in a request always takes the full pipeline. See **BuilderForce: Pipeline Route Report**.
config.pipeline.routing.auto: Score each request and take the quick pass below the route threshold.
config.pipeline.routing.always: Every run takes the full pipeline (the score is still recorded).
config.pipeline.routeThreshold.desc: Router score (0–1, the likelihood a request needs the full pipeline) at or above which a run takes the full pipeline. Lower it if quick runs keep needing a re-run; the route report suggests a value.
config.pipeline.quickModel.desc: Model a **quick pass** codes on. It replaces a soft default — the coding-stage model, `#builderforce.defaultModel#` or the project's learned model — but never a model you picked explicitly for the chat. Empty: the coding-stage model (`#builderforce.models.code#`), else the gateway's order.
config.maxRunBudgetUsd.desc: Spend cap per run, in US dollars (0 = off). The run is warned at 80% and stops at the cap with a summary of what it did; nothing is rolled back. Priced from the bundled price list; models on this machine cost nothing.
config.images.maxEdge.desc: Longest edge, in pixels, an attached picture is scaled to before it is sent to the model (vision models downsample larger pictures anyway). Smaller PNG, WebP and JPEG pictures and every GIF are sent as they are.
config.images.jpegQuality.desc: First quality (0.3–1) tried when an attached picture has to be re-encoded (JPEG, or WebP when it has transparency); lower steps follow only if it is still too large to send inline.
